title: Bandwidth-fair communication splitting and NCCL stream coalescing to reduce tail latency in tensor-parallel serving
author: Sana Patel
description: Motivation: In multi-GPU tensor-parallel serving we observed p99 spikes caused by uneven per-slice transfer times and excessive per-op stream overhead on small collectives. This PR implements a bandwidth-fair splitting strategy for large allreduce/allgather payloads plus an NCCL stream coalescer to reduce kernel/launch overhead. Goals: (1) reduce tail latency and jitter for TP workloads without sacrificing throughput, (2) improve overlap of comm/compute by giving the scheduler richer progress hooks, (3) keep changes compatible with existing rollout and comm topologies. Design summary: Introduces a BandwidthFairSplitter that divides a collective payload into shards proportional to measured link-bandwidth and recent throughput per-peer instead of equal fixed chunks. Each shard is mapped to a dedicated NCCL communicator where beneficial; the mapping is adaptive and bounded so we never create more than 4 communicators per tensor by default. To reduce stream proliferation we add a StreamCoalescer that groups small NCCL ops onto a small pool of cuda streams and merges adjacent launches when they share execution properties. The scheduler receives progress callbacks from both splitter and coalescer and provides a lightweight priority token to prefer outstanding comm shards that are blocking compute. KV cache interaction: added a prefetch-aware sync point so that cross-node KV fetch work is placed before low-priority shards to avoid head-of-line stalls when cache misses coincide with large collectives. Continuous batching: micro-batch slicing allows earlier dispatch of high-priority shards while the rest of the batch aggregates, enabling additional overlap. Backwards compatibility: new behavior is opt-in via runtime config flags (tp.bandwidth_fair_split=true, tp.stream_coalesce=true) with safe defaults matching previous behavior. Testing & results: microbench run on 8xA100 (DGX-style), TP=8 and TP=16 across 70B and 8B models. Results: median latency -12% to -18%, p95 -14% to -21%, p99 reduced up to 25% on noisy hosts; end-to-end throughput improved 5-9% on mixed 8B/70B workloads. Perf tests run in perf-canary and benchmark-lab; canary ID: perf/2026-02-22/tp-split-01. Risks & mitigations: communicator creation can add overhead; we cap communicator churn and reuse communicators per-tenant. Coalescing may hide per-op failures so we added stronger error propagation hooks and CI integration. Rollout plan: staged feature flag rollout per-customer, enable in perf canary, then 10% prod, monitor p99 and token backlog metrics. Checklist: [x] design doc updated, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests in perf lab, [x] canary run, [x] migration safe defaults. Related: ENG-1374 implements telemetry hooks used by the splitter.

patch_snippet: --- a/redwood/runtime/comm/bandwidth_splitter.py +++ b/redwood/runtime/comm/bandwidth_splitter.py @@ def _compute_shards(payload_size, peers): - # naive equal split - shard_size = payload_size // len(peers) + return [shard_size] * len(peers) +# bandwidth-fair split computed from probe samples +weights = _measure_peer_bandwidth(peers) +total = sum(weights) +shards = [max(1, int(payload_size * w // total)) for w in weights] +return shards
review_comments: Liam Chen (reviewer): Can you add a microbenchmark that measures communicator creation overhead for small payloads? Concern is churn when shards are small.
Sana Patel (author): Added canary bench and capped communicator count to 4 by default, see tools/perf/canaries/perf-tp-split.yaml. Communicator reuse logic included in stream_coalescer.cc.
Ana Rodrigues (reviewer): Please ensure the coalescer keeps correct gpu stream ordering for CUDA events used elsewhere in runtime.
Sana Patel (author): Coalescer exposes an ordering API and we added explicit event insertion where needed; unit tests validate event fences.
Marcus Bell (reviewer): Would like to see more telemetry on shard imbalance to tune defaults, consider exposing per-tenant knob.
Sana Patel (author): Telemetry hooks emitted via ENG-1374; added per-tenant config in defaults.yaml and doc notes for ops.
release_notes: Introduce bandwidth-fair collective splitting and NCCL stream coalescing to improve TP tail latency and throughput. Feature gated by tp.bandwidth_fair_split and tp.stream_coalesce. Default off for tenants with custom topologies. See design doc for tuning guidance.
